    Key Enriched Pathways (Top 10)

    1. Factor: IRF; motif: NNGAAANTGAAANN; match class: 1 (TF:M08887_1)

    Agent Summary: Interferon regulatory factor represents a family of sequence-specific transcriptional regulators that bind deoxyribonucleic acid motifs enriched in guanine and adenine residues, including the consensus-like element described here. Key proteins: ACVRL1, CCN3, CD14.
    Read Context ▽

    Interferon regulatory factor represents a family of sequence-specific transcriptional regulators that bind deoxyribonucleic acid motifs enriched in guanine and adenine residues, including the consensus-like element described here. These regulators are central components of innate and adaptive immune signaling.

    2. Factor: p53; motif: NGRCATGYCCAGRCATGYCY; match class: 1 (TF:M10023_1)

    Agent Summary: The pathway described here centers on the transcription factor tumor protein fifty three and its recognition of a canonical deoxyribonucleic acid response element represented by the motif NGRCATGYCCAGRCATGYCY. Key proteins: EDA2R, GDF15, GGT1.
    Read Context ▽

    The pathway described here centers on the transcription factor tumor protein fifty three and its recognition of a canonical deoxyribonucleic acid response element represented by the motif NGRCATGYCCAGRCATGYCY. Tumor protein fifty three is a sequence specific transcriptional regulator that is activated by diverse forms of cellular stress, including deoxyribonucleic acid damage, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, metabolic disturbance, and excitotoxic injury.

    3. Abnormal pleura morphology (HP:0002103)

    Agent Summary: Abnormal pleura morphology refers to structural alterations of the pulmonary pleura, the mesothelial membrane that envelops the lungs and lines the thoracic cavity. Key proteins: AGR2, ELN, EPHB4.
    Read Context ▽

    Abnormal pleura morphology refers to structural alterations of the pulmonary pleura, the mesothelial membrane that envelops the lungs and lines the thoracic cavity. Although this pathway is anatomically centered in the thorax rather than the brain, the pleura is biologically integrated with systemic immune signaling, vascular permeability, inflammatory cytokine production, and tissue remodeling.

    4. Bone pain (HP:0002653)

    Agent Summary: Bone pain is an unpleasant sensory and affective experience localized to osseous tissue and commonly described as aching, throbbing, stabbing, or deep persistent discomfort. Key proteins: FGF23, PSAP, SCARB2.
    Read Context ▽

    Bone pain is an unpleasant sensory and affective experience localized to osseous tissue and commonly described as aching, throbbing, stabbing, or deep persistent discomfort. It arises in diverse clinical settings, including degenerative spine disease, cancer involving bone, chronic kidney disease mineral and bone disorder, osteoporosis, fracture repair, and rare skeletal disorders. Although it is experienced at the level of the skeleton, bone pain is not a purely local phenomenon.

    5. carbohydrate binding (GO:0030246)

    Agent Summary: Carbohydrate binding is a molecular function in which a protein selectively and non-covalently recognizes carbohydrate structures, including simple sugars, complex oligosaccharides, polysaccharides, and chemically modified sugar derivatives. Key proteins: AMBP, CLEC4D, COLEC12.
    Read Context ▽

    Carbohydrate binding is a molecular function in which a protein selectively and non-covalently recognizes carbohydrate structures, including simple sugars, complex oligosaccharides, polysaccharides, and chemically modified sugar derivatives. This function is biologically important because carbohydrates are major components of the cell surface and extracellular environment, where they regulate cell adhesion, receptor activation, immune recognition, trafficking, and intercellular communication.

    8. symbiont entry into host cell (GO:0046718)

    Agent Summary: Symbiont entry into host cell refers to the biological process by which a non-host organism, or its genetic material, crosses the host plasma membrane and becomes established within the host cell. Key proteins: ITGAV, LGALS1, LGALS9.
    Read Context ▽

    Symbiont entry into host cell refers to the biological process by which a non-host organism, or its genetic material, crosses the host plasma membrane and becomes established within the host cell. In the literature provided, this process is represented mainly by microbial or viral entry events that depend on specific host surface receptors, proteases, membrane remodeling, and immune tolerance mechanisms.

    9. lipid localization (GO:0010876)

    Agent Summary: Lipid localization refers to the set of biological processes that transport lipids to defined cellular or tissue compartments, retain them there, and dynamically redistribute them when physiological conditions change. Key proteins: MDK, TREM2.
    Read Context ▽

    Lipid localization refers to the set of biological processes that transport lipids to defined cellular or tissue compartments, retain them there, and dynamically redistribute them when physiological conditions change. This pathway includes the movement and compartmentalization of membrane phospholipids, sphingolipids, cholesterol-rich membrane microdomains, fatty acids, and bioactive lipid mediators across organelles, membranes, endosomes, synapses, glial membranes, and extracellular interfaces.

    The cytokine and inflammatory response pathway comprises a coordinated network of immune signaling molecules, their receptors, intracellular transcriptional regulators, inflammasome machinery, and cellular effectors that together detect danger signals and orchestrate host defense, tissue adaptation, and repair.
